cards.text: Friend, the skilled craftsmen get to work on the tabernacle. First up: ten curtains of finely spun linen, with blue, purple and scarlet yarn. Grab your apron, because these folks are about to out-craft every craft fair you've ever walked through.

cards.question: The ten curtains for the tabernacle are linen and colored yarn. What's skillfully worked into them?

cards.text: The ten curtains get joined into two sets of five, with fifty loops of blue material along the edge of each set, lined up across from each other. FIFTY loops lined up perfectly, and I can't line up twelve cookies on a tray without one rolling off to start a new life.

cards.question: To link the loops on the two sets of linen curtains, the craftsmen make fifty gold clasps. What do the clasps do for the tabernacle?

cards.text: Over the tabernacle goes a tent made of goat hair, eleven curtains in all, every one the same size.

cards.question: The eleven goat hair curtains get joined into two sets. One set has five curtains, and the other set has ___.
Each set of goat hair curtains gets ___ loops along its edge, the same way the linen sets did.

cards.text: Then come fifty clasps to join the goat hair tent, and this time they're bronze, not gold. Over the whole tent go two more coverings: ram skins dyed red, and over that, fine leather.

Then come the walls: upright frames of acacia wood, twenty on the south side, twenty on the north and more across the back, each one standing on two silver bases. Crossbars run along the frames, and the frames and crossbars all get overlaid with gold.
Next comes the veil, made from the same blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen as the ten curtains. This crew has gone through more yarn than a craft store on clearance day.

cards.question: True or false: the veil is made from the same materials as the ten curtains, and it has cherubim skillfully worked into it too.

cards.text: The veil hangs on four acacia posts overlaid with gold, with gold hooks. Then comes an embroidered curtain for the entrance to the tent, held up by five posts.

cards.question: Like the tabernacle's wall frames, the veil's four posts stand on ___ bases.
The veil's posts stand on silver bases. The five posts at the tent's entrance get bases of a different metal. What is it?

cards.text: Now Bezalel, the lead craftsman, builds the ark out of acacia wood. He overlays it with pure gold, inside and out.

cards.question: Bezalel casts four gold rings for the ark's four feet and makes poles overlaid with gold. What are the poles for?

cards.text: Then he makes the mercy seat out of pure gold, with the same length and width as the ark. A gold ark and a solid gold mercy seat, while my fanciest address for years was the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: At each end of the mercy seat, Bezalel hammers something out of gold. What is it?
True or false: the two cherubim on the mercy seat spread their wings upward and face each other, looking toward the mercy seat.

cards.text: Next he makes a table of acacia wood, overlaid with pure gold, with gold rings and gold-covered poles for carrying it. That's two pieces now built with carrying poles, and I RESPECT furniture that's ready to travel, because I sat in one drawer for YEARS.

cards.question: Bezalel makes the utensils for the gold table out of pure gold too. What are they?

cards.text: Then he makes the lampstand out of pure hammered gold. Six branches come out of its sides, three on one side and three on the other.

cards.question: Each branch of the lampstand gets three cups shaped like ___ blossoms.
True or false: the lampstand's buds and branches are made separately and attached to it afterward.
The lampstand has six branches, three on each side, plus the lampstand itself. Bezalel makes ___ lamps for it.

cards.text: The lampstand and all its utensils come from a talent of pure gold. That is a LOT of shine, friend.
Next comes a small square altar of acacia wood, a cubit long and a cubit wide. He overlays it with pure gold and gives it gold rings and poles for carrying it.

cards.question: After the lampstand, Bezalel makes a small square altar of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold. What is that altar for?

cards.text: He also makes the sacred anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer. Build an ark, hammer a lampstand AND mix a fragrance? On my best day, I stamp a cookie.
Bezalel builds the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood, square, five cubits long, five cubits wide and three cubits high. This is not the little incense altar, friend, this one is BIG.

cards.question: At each of the altar's four corners, Bezalel makes a ___.
The ark, the table and the incense altar all got pure gold. What does Bezalel overlay the altar of burnt offering with?

cards.text: All the altar's utensils are bronze too: pots, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans. Then a bronze mesh grate goes under its ledge, halfway up from the bottom.

cards.question: True or false: like the ark and the table, the altar of burnt offering has rings and poles for carrying it.
True or false: the altar of burnt offering is solid wood all the way through.

cards.text: Next comes the bronze basin and its stand. And the bronze for it comes from somewhere you would NOT expect.

cards.question: Where does the bronze for the basin and its stand come from?

cards.text: Those women served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and their MIRRORS became the basin. I've got a mustache this size, friend, so I know exactly what kind of sacrifice that is.

Then he builds the courtyard all around, with curtains of finely spun linen, a hundred cubits on the south and north sides and fifty on the west and east. The posts stand on bronze bases with silver hooks and bands, the entrance gets an embroidered curtain, and every tent peg is bronze.

Then comes the inventory, recorded at Moses' command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest. After all the old receipts I shared that drawer with, these are the first records I've ever been excited about.

cards.question: The inventory names Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, as the one who made everything the LORD had commanded Moses. Which tribe is Bezalel from?
Working with Bezalel is Oholiab son of Ahisamach, an engraver and designer from the tribe of ___.

cards.text: Then come the totals of gold, silver and bronze, and the silver comes from half a shekel for each of 603,550 men, enough to cast a hundred silver bases. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this build is not done yet.

findings.problem: Almost the whole passage is construction detail: curtain counts and sizes, loops, clasps, frames, bases, furnishings and courtyard measurements. prep-walkthrough.md lists building plans for the tabernacle as a long stretch, which gets one summary story card and never a choice card. The walkthrough summarizes only two parts this way (36:20-34 and 38:9-20). It asks choice cards on other build details of the same kind, such as goat hair curtain counts, loop counts and base metals (stop 1 cards 6, 7, 13, 14).
findings.question: When a whole passage, or nearly all of it, is the kind of detail the docs call a long stretch (here, the tabernacle being built), how should Prep handle it? A stretch can't have a stop of its own or any choice cards, but Prep still needs stops with at least as many choice cards as story cards. Which build details, if any, may get choice cards, and which must be folded into summary story cards?

findings.problem: Card 3 already said the linen sets had fifty loops. The question then says 'the same way the linen sets did,' which hands the baker the answer instead of letting them reason to it.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 9 said each wall frame stands on silver bases. The question opens with 'Like the tabernacle's wall frames,' which gives away that the veil's bases are silver.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says the mercy seat has 'the same length and width as the ark.' That comparison uses the ark's measurements in 37:1, but the card cites only 37:6.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question explains seven lamps as six branches 'plus the lampstand itself.' The text never says where the lamps sit or that they match the branches plus the shaft. This adds a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The only humor is 'That is a LOT of shine, friend.' It reads as a pleasant remark, not a real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. Only the opening card may have up to 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question first says the ark, the table and the incense altar 'all got pure gold,' then asks what this altar is overlaid with. The contrast signals the answer isn't gold, which rules out a wrong answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Calling the mirrors 'that kind of sacrifice' suggests the women gave them up willingly or at a cost. Exodus 38:8 only says the basin was made from their mirrors. It doesn't say how the mirrors were given or why.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The mustache-and-mirror joke needs an unstated step: a big mustache needs a mirror, so giving up a mirror is hard. It doesn't click instantly, and it leans toward a joke about appearance.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line, 'And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend,' nearly copies the example line in the docs instead of being written fresh.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
